newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Coconut oil prices seen sliding from 10-year high.
newsitem.headline: Coconut oil prices seen sliding from 10-year high.

text.p: Coconut oil prices are expected to soften in early 1997 on prospects of better harvests in the Philippines after hitting a 10-year high in June, vegetable oil traders in Manila said on Monday.

"The market's inactivity this month may result in accumulation of copra and oil from origin sellers which may create selling pressure in early January," said a senior trader with Philippine food and beverage giant San Miguel Corp.
The trader said he expected coconut oil prices to be either steady or $5 to $10 lower in Rotterdam in the first week of January.
"However, the slide may be temporary as it will just be a flushing out of those in the long," the SMC trader said.
Other Manila brokers said they expected prices to be generally lower for most of 1997.

Data from the trade group United Coconut Association of the Philippines Inc (UCAP) showed average monthly prices of the country's coconut oil exports hit $830 per tonne FOB in June, the highest prices since fetching $839 in January 1985.
In a report last week, UCAP said it expected coconut exports to rise next year as local harvests recover from typhoon damage.

The coconut crop in the Philippines, the world's largest exporter of coconut oil, is expected to rise by 8.9 percent to 2.142 million tonnes in copra terms in 1997 from this year's forecast 1.966 million tonnes, UCAP said.
UCAP had lowered its crop forecast for 1996 to 1.966 million tonnes from an earlier 2.334 million.
"For 1997, it is projected that production is to slightly recover owing to this year's good precipitation levels," it added.
Philippine coconut output hit a record 2.648 million tonnes in 1995, UCAP said.

"The very low export turnout since the start of the year has only demonstrated that the twin effects of last year's typhoon damage and stressed trees undergoing recovery from heavy fruiting have been more severe than anticipated," it said.
Copra exports in 1997 were forecast to reach 1.536 million tonnes, the bulk of which would be coconut oil, it said.
The group said it expected coconut exports to fall to 1.426 million tonnes in 1996 from the year-earlier 2.265 million tonnes.
Exports of coconut oil alone are seen reaching 900,000 tonnes in 1997, up from this year's forecast of 840,000 tonnes, but down from 1995's 1.34 million tonnes.

"Gauging from the rainfall pattern this year, it is anticipated that export volumes during the first semester next year would be bigger, representing 53 percent of the annual total, compared to the second semester tonnage," UCAP said.
Enrique Uy, president of E.U. and Sons Trading Corp, and another Manila broker agreed with the UCAP forecast of better harvests in early 1997.
"I agree that there will be an increase in 1997," said Uy, adding that the absence of major typhoon damage in coconut-growing areas in 1996 should boost production.
Another Manila trader, however, said prospects of higher coconut oil exports next year would depend on the availability of more ships.

He said unless there is a large quantity of oil produced, ship owners will continue to prefer to pick up palm and coconut oil from Indonesia because they don't have to collect it from several ports there as they do in the Philippines.
